reconstructed_theorem_text: For all real-valued functions interpolation and interpolation' and all real rate, s, and t, if s ≤ t, interpolation has derivative interpolation'(u) at every u ∈ [s,t], and rate·interpolation(u) ≤ interpolation'(u) for every u ∈ (s,t), then interpolation(s) ≤ interpolation(t)·exp(-rate·(t-s)). The endpoint derivative hypotheses are genuine two-sided HasDerivAt statements; s=t is allowed; rate and the function values have no sign restrictions; behavior outside [s,t] is unconstrained.
objects: Two real-valued functions interpolation, interpolation' and three real parameters rate, s, t.
domains: interpolation, interpolation' : ℝ → ℝ; rate, s, t : ℝ.
quantifiers: All objects are universally quantified; the derivative identity ranges over Icc s t and the growth bound over Ioo s t.
assumptions: s≤t; HasDerivAt interpolation (interpolation' u) u on [s,t]; rate*interpolation(u)≤interpolation'(u) on (s,t).
scopes: Endpoint derivatives are genuine two-sided derivatives; growth is interior-only; s=t is allowed; behavior outside [s,t] is unconstrained.
constant_dependencies: The exponent is exactly -rate*(t-s); rate and function values have no sign restrictions.
